paragraphs.title: The Coming Destruction and Babylon's Retribution

answers: Babylon and those dwelling in her midst
easy.explanation: The LORD raises a destroying wind against Babylon and her inhabitants.
easy.q: Against whom does the LORD raise a destroying wind?

answers: Fan her and empty her land
easy.explanation: The fanners will scatter Babylon and empty her land.
easy.q: What will the fanners do to Babylon?

easy.explanation: The passage says not to spare her young men and to destroy her host utterly.
easy.q: What are Babylon's young men and host commanded to receive?

answers: The time of the LORD's vengeance has come
medium.explanation: They are told to flee because the LORD will render recompence to Babylon.
medium.q: Why are God's people told to flee from Babylon?

answers: Babylon made the nations drunk through her influence and evil
medium.explanation: Babylon's influence spread corruption among the nations like wine from a cup.
medium.q: What does the image of Babylon as a golden cup in the LORD's hand mean?

answers: Babylon's condition could not be repaired and judgment was certain
medium.explanation: Babylon's judgment had reached heaven, so the nations were told to forsake her.
medium.q: What does the statement, “We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed,” show?

answers: Babylon will be repaid for the evil she did in Zion
Babylon will be spared because of her strength
Israel will be punished instead of Babylon
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to repay Babylon for the evil she did in Zion.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Babylon's treatment of Zion and her punishment?

answers: The fulfillment of divine judgment despite her power
Her return to rule over the nations
challenge.explanation: Her sudden fall shows that Babylon's power cannot prevent God's judgment.
challenge.q: What does Babylon's sudden fall demonstrate?

answers: Israel has not been forsaken by their God, while Babylon is judged for her guilt
Israel is the destructive power and Babylon is the victim
challenge.explanation: Israel has not been forsaken, but Babylon faces judgment for her sins.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Israel and Babylon?

paragraphs.title: The Lord, Creator of the World, and His Weapon

answers: As the builder of Babylon's walls
As the maker of the earth and establisher of the world
easy.explanation: The LORD made the earth, established the world, and stretched out the heavens.
easy.q: How is the LORD described in these verses?

easy.explanation: The molten images are false and have no breath in them.
easy.q: What is described as false and without breath?

easy.explanation: The LORD has raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes.
easy.q: Whose spirit has the LORD raised against Babylon?

answers: It shows that Babylon's idols have creative power
It presents the LORD as supreme in power over creation
It teaches that Babylon created the heavens
medium.explanation: The LORD controls the earth, heavens, rain, and wind, unlike powerless idols.
medium.q: How does the description of creation strengthen the message about Babylon?

answers: A person proves foolish when trusting in an idol
medium.explanation: The verse calls people foolish for trusting in false images.
medium.q: What does “Every man is brutish by his knowledge” mean in context?

answers: As an instrument used to break nations and kingdoms
As a tool for building the temple
As a weapon to defend Babylon forever
medium.explanation: The LORD used Babylon to break nations, but He will also break Babylon.
medium.q: How is Babylon used as a “battle axe and weapons of war”?

answers: The idols create the world, while the LORD is powerless
The LORD creates and governs the world, while idols are vanity and falsehood
challenge.explanation: The LORD is the Creator, while idols are empty works of error.
challenge.q: What contrast between the LORD and idols is emphasized?

answers: An instrument used by God is not immune from judgment
The LORD does not control kingdoms
challenge.explanation: Although Babylon served as an instrument, she was still accountable for her evil.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the LORD using Babylon as a weapon and then breaking her?

answers: The LORD controls only the clouds
The LORD controls creation and also raises kings to judge Babylon
The kings act independently of God
challenge.explanation: The Creator who controls nature also directs the kings of the Medes against Babylon.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between God's control of nature and history?

easy.explanation: Babylon is called the destroying mountain that destroys the whole earth.
easy.q: What is Babylon called at the beginning of this section?

easy.explanation: The nations of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz are specifically named.
easy.q: Which peoples are summoned against Babylon?

answers: Their might fails and they stop fighting
easy.explanation: The mighty men remain in their strongholds, and their might fails.
easy.q: What happens to Babylon's mighty men?

answers: Babylon, which destroyed the earth, will become a burnt mountain
Babylon will be rebuilt upon the mountain
medium.explanation: The LORD will roll Babylon down and make her a burnt mountain.
medium.q: What is the meaning of the destroying-mountain image?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that Babylon's warriors lost their strength.
medium.q: What does “their might hath failed” mean?

answers: Babylon is approaching the time of judgment
Babylon is occupied only with farming
medium.explanation: The threshingfloor image points to Babylon's approaching punishment.
medium.q: What does the image of Babylon as a threshingfloor awaiting harvest suggest?

answers: The nations are summoned, and then reports come that the city is taken
The city is saved before the army arrives
The passage gives no sense of progress
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from gathering the nations to the capture and collapse of the city.
challenge.q: How does the passage describe the movement from preparation to execution of the campaign?

answers: The collapse of Babylon's defensive power
Their earlier conquest of other cities
challenge.explanation: Their failed might and broken bars show that Babylon's defenses are collapsing.
challenge.q: What does the inability of Babylon's mighty men to fight signify?

answers: Walls, warriors, passages, reeds, and fighting men are all affected
challenge.explanation: The judgment includes the city's defenses, passages, structures, and army.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that destruction reaches every part of Babylon?

easy.explanation: The daughter of Zion describes being devoured, crushed, and emptied.
easy.q: Who describes the harm suffered from Nebuchadrezzar?

answers: Plead their cause and take vengeance
easy.explanation: The LORD promises to plead their cause and take vengeance for them.
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to do for Zion and Jerusalem?

answers: Heaps and a desolate place without an inhabitant
easy.explanation: Babylon will become heaps, a dwelling place for dragons, and a desolation.

answers: As the action of a kind shepherd
As devouring, crushing, swallowing, and emptying her
medium.explanation: Jerusalem portrays Nebuchadrezzar as one who violently consumed and cast her out.
medium.q: How does Jerusalem describe Nebuchadrezzar's treatment of her?

answers: Babylon will receive payment in judgment for her deeds
Babylon will receive a reward for righteousness
Jerusalem will pay tribute to Babylon
medium.explanation: A recompence is a fitting repayment for Babylon's evil.
medium.q: What does “I will render unto her a recompence” mean?

answers: The completion of her devastation and isolation
Only the transfer of her capital
medium.explanation: The absence of inhabitants emphasizes the completeness of Babylon's ruin.
medium.q: What does Babylon becoming a place without an inhabitant symbolize?

answers: Her punishment is presented as a direct response to the violence done in Zion
challenge.explanation: The LORD takes vengeance because Babylon harmed Jerusalem and Zion.
challenge.q: How are Babylon's violence and her punishment connected?

answers: Even Babylon's god is defeated and cannot save her
challenge.explanation: The LORD will bring out what Bel swallowed and end the nations' devotion to him.
challenge.q: What is the significance of Bel being judged?

answers: She changes from a famous empire into a ruined and empty city
She changes from ruin into a great empire
She changes from idolatry to worship of the LORD
challenge.explanation: Babylon's former glory is replaced by desolation and the defeat of her god.
challenge.q: What sharp change in Babylon's status is described?

paragraphs.title: A Call to the Exiles and Hope for Removing Shame

easy.explanation: The LORD tells His people to leave Babylon and save every man his soul.
easy.q: Who is told to go out from the midst of Babylon?

answers: The rumour heard in the land
easy.explanation: They are told not to let their hearts faint because of the rumors.
easy.q: What are God's people told not to fear?

answers: The images will be judged and the wall will fall
They will be moved to Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The LORD will judge Babylon's images, and Babylon's wall will fall.
easy.q: What will happen to Babylon's graven images and walls?

answers: To escape the fierce anger of the LORD
medium.explanation: They are told to leave so they will not perish in Babylon's iniquity.
medium.q: Why are the Israelites called to leave Babylon?

answers: Babylon will celebrate and rise again
The rulers and warriors will fall into a final, irreversible death
medium.explanation: The image describes the final downfall of Babylon's leaders and warriors.
medium.q: What does “sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake” mean?

medium.explanation: Jerusalem says that strangers have entered the sanctuaries and covered her with shame.
medium.q: How does Jerusalem respond to the report of the temple's profanation?

answers: Leaving Babylon involves both physical escape and renewed remembrance of God and Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Those who escape are told to remember the LORD afar off and let Jerusalem come to mind.
challenge.q: What connection is made between leaving Babylon and remembering the LORD and Jerusalem?

answers: Fear may increase through repeated rumors, but God's people are told not to faint
challenge.explanation: The passage acknowledges repeated reports but urges the exiles not to lose courage.
challenge.q: What message arises from the repeated rumors and passing years?

answers: From high walls and strength to defeat, burning, and desolation
From military strength to rule over Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Babylon's proud strength is contrasted with the coming destruction of her walls and land.
challenge.q: How is Babylon's reversal of fortune portrayed?

paragraphs.title: The Book, the Stone, and the Sinking in the River

easy.explanation: Jeremiah gave the book to Seraiah, the son of Neriah.
easy.q: To whom did Jeremiah give the book?

answers: See the place and read all the words
easy.explanation: Seraiah was commanded to read all the words written against Babylon.
easy.q: What was Seraiah to do when he came to Babylon?

answers: He tied a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates
He placed it on Babylon's wall
He gave it to Babylon's king
easy.explanation: He was commanded to bind a stone to the book and cast it into the Euphrates.
easy.q: What did Seraiah do after reading the book?

answers: Only the history of Judah's kings
All the evil that would come upon Babylon
medium.explanation: The book contained the words of judgment against Babylon.

answers: To make the book sink in the water
To preserve the book in a treasury
medium.explanation: The stone would cause the book to sink into the Euphrates.
medium.q: What was the purpose of tying a stone to the book?

answers: Babylon will sink and not rise from the evil brought upon her
Babylon will become stronger through the river
Babylon will be cleansed from sin
medium.explanation: The action symbolizes the declaration that Babylon will sink and not rise.
medium.q: What does the sinking of the book declare about Babylon's future?

answers: The sinking book illustrates Babylon's own sinking
challenge.explanation: The book's descent into the river visibly represents Babylon's downfall.
challenge.q: How does the action with the book turn the prophecy into a tangible symbol?

answers: He is the witness and executor of Jeremiah's command in Babylon
challenge.explanation: Seraiah receives the book, reads it, and carries out the symbolic act.
challenge.q: What is Seraiah's role in the conclusion?

answers: The written prophecy is read, and then an action symbolizes its fulfillment
The action replaces all the prophetic words
The words and action are unrelated
challenge.explanation: Reading the book and sinking it in the Euphrates join the message to a visible sign.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion connect spoken prophecy with action?
